subject_session: sub-LA3_ses-3 (prototype) + all 15 sessions (5 mice); population pooled
stated_limitation: By construction the value at 0 octaves is 1.0 for every unit (that is where its own maximum is), so the curve's peak is not itself informative; what demonstrates genuine band-pass frequency tuning is the systematic, roughly symmetric fall-off in response at +/-1 and +/-2 octaves from BF.

justification.dataset: 000986 is the canonical pure-tone auditory-cortex Neuropixels dataset, exactly right for frequency tuning.
justification.handling: Real data streamed and correctly aligned with sensible evoked/baseline windows, but no spike-sorting quality criteria are applied to unit selection.
justification.analysis: One-way ANOVA across the five frequency groups is appropriate and correct, though no multiple-comparison correction across units is discussed (the effect is far above chance so the conclusion holds).
justification.correctness: Numbers reproduce deterministically and are internally consistent (85.6% of 1564 = 1339 tuned units matches fig5B; the 82% in fig5A is the distinct mean-of-session-fractions).
justification.figures: Figures show the effect clearly with labeled axes, units, and sample sizes; examples are selected by significance and the population BF-aligned curve is honestly annotated.
justification.honesty: Nothing is misrepresented and the fig5C construction caveat is sophisticated, but the write-up names no result-specific limitations (unit quality, passive single-amplitude paradigm) on an otherwise clean result.
justification.verdict: Canonical dataset, correct pipeline, reproducible and internally consistent numbers, clear figures, and no overstatement: an accept with minor optional revisions.
